title: SQL Injection
description: User input is improperly included in SQL queries, allowing attackers to access, modify, or delete database records without authorization.
remediation: Use parameterized queries, prepared statements, and input validation. Restrict database permissions and avoid dynamic query construction.

title: Blind SQL Injection
description: Attackers can infer database information by observing application responses even when query results are not directly displayed.
remediation: Implement parameterized queries, generic error messages, and continuous security testing to identify injection flaws.

title: Time-Based SQL Injection
description: Attackers use database delay functions to determine whether injected SQL statements are executed successfully.
remediation: Prevent SQL injection through prepared statements, input validation, and monitoring of abnormal query execution times.

title: NoSQL Injection
description: Improper handling of user input allows manipulation of NoSQL queries, potentially exposing sensitive information.
remediation: Validate user input, avoid dynamic query generation, and enforce strict authentication and authorization controls.

title: LDAP Injection
description: Unvalidated input may alter LDAP queries, allowing attackers to bypass authentication or access directory data.
remediation: Escape special LDAP characters, validate inputs, and use parameterized LDAP query mechanisms.

title: XPath Injection
description: Improperly validated input can manipulate XPath queries and expose sensitive XML data or bypass authentication controls.
remediation: Validate user input, use parameterized XPath expressions, and avoid dynamic query construction.

title: OS Command Injection
description: Attackers can execute unauthorized operating system commands through unsanitized user input.
remediation: Avoid shell execution where possible, validate inputs strictly, and use secure APIs instead of system commands.

title: Code Injection
description: Untrusted input is interpreted as executable code, allowing attackers to alter application behavior.
remediation: Remove dynamic code execution, validate all inputs, and follow secure coding practices.

title: Expression Language Injection
description: Attackers can manipulate expression language statements to execute unauthorized operations within applications.
remediation: Disable unnecessary expression evaluation and sanitize all user-controlled input.

title: Template Injection (SSTI)
description: Malicious input can be executed within server-side templates, leading to data exposure or code execution.
remediation: Use secure template configurations and prevent user-controlled template content.

title: CRLF Injection
description: Attackers inject CRLF characters to manipulate HTTP responses, logs, or application behavior.
remediation: Validate and sanitize input data before including it in headers or responses.

title: XML Injection
description: Improper handling of XML input may allow attackers to alter application logic or access unauthorized data.
remediation: Validate XML input, use secure parsers, and restrict processing of untrusted XML content.

title: JSON Injection
description: Malicious manipulation of JSON structures can alter application behavior and bypass security controls.
remediation: Validate JSON data structures and enforce strict schema validation for API requests.

title: Header Injection
description: Improperly sanitized input can modify HTTP headers and affect application responses or redirects.
remediation: Sanitize user input and restrict dynamic header generation wherever possible.

title: Log Injection
description: Attackers can manipulate log entries to hide malicious activity or create misleading audit records.
remediation: Sanitize logged data, encode special characters, and protect log integrity through monitoring.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Malicious scripts can be injected into web pages and executed in a user's browser, leading to data theft or session compromise.
remediation: Sanitize user input, encode output properly, and implement a strong Content Security Policy (CSP).

title: Stored XSS
description: Malicious scripts are permanently stored by the application and executed whenever affected users view the content.
remediation: Validate and sanitize all stored content, encode output, and perform regular security testing.

title: Reflected XSS
description: Malicious scripts are reflected from user input and executed immediately when a victim accesses a crafted request.
remediation: Validate request parameters, encode output, and avoid rendering untrusted input directly in responses.

title: DOM-Based XSS
description: The vulnerability occurs within client-side scripts when untrusted input modifies the Document Object Model (DOM).
remediation: Avoid unsafe DOM manipulation methods and sanitize data before inserting it into page content.

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
description: Attackers can trick authenticated users into performing unintended actions on trusted applications.
remediation: Implement CSRF tokens, use SameSite cookies, and verify request origins before processing actions.

title: Clickjacking
description: Users are tricked into clicking hidden or disguised elements, causing unintended actions within applications.
remediation: Use X-Frame-Options and Content Security Policy frame restrictions to prevent unauthorized framing.

title: Open Redirect
description: Users can be redirected to malicious websites through improperly validated redirect parameters.
remediation: Validate redirect destinations against approved allowlists and avoid user-controlled redirect URLs.

title: Content Spoofing
description: Attackers manipulate displayed content to mislead users, impersonate trusted information, or facilitate phishing attacks.
remediation: Validate displayed content, implement integrity checks, and restrict user-controlled rendering where possible.

title: Broken Authentication
description: Weak or improperly implemented authentication mechanisms may allow attackers to gain unauthorized access to user accounts and sensitive resources.
remediation: Implement secure authentication controls, enforce strong passwords, and monitor login activities for suspicious behavior.

title: Weak Password Policy
description: Insufficient password requirements increase the risk of brute-force attacks and unauthorized account compromise.
remediation: Enforce minimum password length, complexity requirements, and periodic password reviews.

title: Default Credentials
description: Systems using vendor-supplied default credentials can be easily compromised by attackers.
remediation: Change all default credentials immediately after deployment and enforce unique account passwords.

title: Hardcoded Credentials
description: Credentials embedded in source code, documents, or configuration files can be exposed and abused by attackers.
remediation: Store secrets in secure vaults or environment variables and rotate exposed credentials immediately.

title: Credential Stuffing
description: Attackers use previously compromised usernames and passwords to gain access to user accounts across multiple services.
remediation: Implement MFA, monitor suspicious login patterns, and enforce protection against automated login attempts.

title: Password Reuse Risk
description: Using the same password across multiple accounts increases the impact of a single credential compromise.
remediation: Encourage unique passwords for every account and provide password manager guidance to users.

title: Missing Multi-Factor Authentication
description: Accounts protected only by passwords are more vulnerable to credential theft and unauthorized access.
remediation: Enable MFA for all critical accounts and require additional verification for sensitive actions.

title: Session Fixation
description: Attackers may force users to authenticate with a known session identifier, enabling account compromise.
remediation: Generate new session identifiers after successful authentication and invalidate old sessions.

title: Session Hijacking
description: Attackers gain access to valid session tokens and impersonate authenticated users.
remediation: Protect session tokens using HTTPS, secure cookie attributes, and session timeout controls.

title: Weak Session Management
description: Poor session handling may allow unauthorized access through predictable or improperly managed sessions.
remediation: Use secure session identifiers, enforce inactivity timeouts, and invalidate sessions after logout.

title: Insecure Password Reset
description: Weak password recovery mechanisms can be exploited to take over legitimate user accounts.
remediation: Use secure reset tokens, expiration periods, identity verification, and audit password reset activities.

title: Excessive Login Attempts
description: Unlimited or excessive login attempts increase the likelihood of successful password guessing attacks.
remediation: Implement rate limiting, account lockout policies, CAPTCHA protections, and login monitoring.

title: Broken Access Control
description: Access restrictions are not properly enforced, allowing users to access resources or functions beyond their intended permissions.
remediation: Implement server-side authorization checks, apply least-privilege principles, and regularly review access control policies.

title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR)
description: Attackers can manipulate identifiers to access data or resources belonging to other users without proper authorization.
remediation: Validate ownership of requested resources and enforce authorization checks for every object access request.

title: Privilege Escalation
description: Attackers gain permissions beyond their assigned role, potentially obtaining administrative or system-level access.
remediation: Apply least-privilege principles, review permission assignments, and monitor for unauthorized privilege changes.

title: Missing Authorization Checks
description: Application functions or resources can be accessed without verifying whether the user has appropriate permissions.
remediation: Perform authorization checks on every sensitive operation and enforce role-based access controls consistently.

title: Horizontal Privilege Escalation
description: Users can access data or perform actions belonging to other users with similar privilege levels.
remediation: Validate user ownership before granting access and implement strict object-level authorization controls.

title: Vertical Privilege Escalation
description: Lower-privileged users can gain access to administrative functions or highly privileged system resources.
remediation: Enforce strict role separation, verify permissions server-side, and audit privileged functionality regularly.

title: Excessive User Permissions
description: Users are granted more permissions than required for their responsibilities, increasing security risks.
remediation: Review user roles periodically and restrict permissions to only those required for job functions.

title: Overprivileged Service Accounts
description: Service accounts possess unnecessary privileges that could be abused if compromised by attackers.
remediation: Assign only required permissions to service accounts and regularly audit privileged account usage.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: Sensitive information is accessible to unauthorized users due to inadequate protection, storage, or transmission controls.
remediation: Encrypt sensitive data, restrict access permissions, and implement secure data handling procedures.

title: API Key Exposure
description: API keys are exposed in documents, code, or configurations, allowing unauthorized access to services and resources.
remediation: Store API keys securely in secret management systems and rotate exposed keys immediately.

title: Secret Token Exposure
description: Authentication or authorization tokens are exposed and may be used to impersonate legitimate users or services.
remediation: Protect tokens in secure storage, limit their lifetime, and revoke compromised tokens promptly.

title: Private Key Exposure
description: Private cryptographic keys are exposed, potentially allowing unauthorized decryption, signing, or system access.
remediation: Store keys securely, restrict access, and replace any keys suspected of being compromised.

title: Certificate Exposure
description: Certificate information is improperly disclosed, increasing the risk of misuse or aiding attacker reconnaissance.
remediation: Restrict certificate access, monitor certificate usage, and manage certificates through approved processes.

title: Password Disclosure
description: Passwords are stored, transmitted, or displayed in an insecure manner, increasing the risk of account compromise.
remediation: Use secure password storage, avoid plaintext exposure, and enforce strong password management policies.

title: Personally Identifiable Information Exposure
description: Personal information such as names, addresses, or identification numbers is exposed to unauthorized parties.
remediation: Apply data classification, encryption, masking, and access controls to protect personal information.

title: Financial Data Exposure
description: Sensitive financial records or payment information are exposed, creating risks of fraud and compliance violations.
remediation: Encrypt financial information, restrict access, and comply with applicable financial security standards.

title: Healthcare Data Exposure
description: Medical or healthcare-related information is exposed without proper protection or authorization controls.
remediation: Protect healthcare records using encryption, access controls, and regulatory compliance measures.

title: Unencrypted Sensitive Data
description: Sensitive information is stored or transmitted without encryption, making it vulnerable to unauthorized access.
remediation: Use strong encryption for data at rest and in transit and implement secure key management practices.

title: Weak Cryptography
description: Outdated or insecure cryptographic methods are used, reducing the effectiveness of data protection mechanisms.
remediation: Use modern cryptographic standards and regularly review encryption implementations.

title: Deprecated Hash Algorithm Usage
description: Older hashing algorithms with known weaknesses are used to protect passwords or sensitive information.
remediation: Replace deprecated hashing algorithms with secure alternatives such as bcrypt, Argon2, or SHA-256.

title: MD5 Usage
description: MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks and should not be used for security-sensitive operations.
remediation: Replace MD5 with stronger hashing algorithms such as SHA-256, bcrypt, or Argon2.

title: SHA1 Usage
description: SHA-1 has known cryptographic weaknesses and is no longer recommended for security-critical use cases.
remediation: Migrate to SHA-256 or stronger cryptographic algorithms for hashing and digital signatures.

title: Weak TLS Configuration
description: TLS settings are improperly configured, potentially allowing downgrade attacks or insecure communications.
remediation: Disable outdated protocols, enforce TLS 1.2 or higher, and follow current security best practices.

title: Insecure Cipher Suites
description: Weak or deprecated cipher suites may expose encrypted communications to interception or cryptographic attacks.
remediation: Disable weak ciphers and allow only strong, industry-approved encryption algorithms.

title: Self-Signed Certificate Usage
description: Self-signed certificates lack trusted validation and may increase the risk of impersonation attacks.
remediation: Use certificates issued by trusted Certificate Authorities and manage certificate lifecycles properly.

title: Certificate Validation Failure
description: Certificate validation checks are missing or improperly implemented, increasing the risk of man-in-the-middle attacks.
remediation: Enforce strict certificate validation and verify certificate trust chains during connections.

title: Improper Key Management
description: Cryptographic keys are not generated, stored, rotated, or protected according to security best practices.
remediation: Implement centralized key management, regular key rotation, and strict access controls for cryptographic keys.

title: Security Misconfiguration
description: Improperly configured systems may expose sensitive functionality, increase attack surface, or weaken security controls.
remediation: Review configurations regularly, disable unnecessary features, and follow security hardening guidelines.

title: Missing Security Headers
description: Required security headers are absent, reducing browser-level protections against common web attacks.
remediation: Implement recommended HTTP security headers and validate configurations through security testing.

title: Missing Content Security Policy
description: The application lacks a Content Security Policy, increasing the risk of script injection attacks.
remediation: Define and enforce a Content Security Policy that restricts trusted content sources.

title: Missing HSTS Header
description: Browsers are not instructed to use secure HTTPS connections, increasing downgrade attack risks.
remediation: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) and enforce HTTPS across all services.

title: Missing X-Frame-Options
description: Pages can be embedded within frames, increasing the risk of clickjacking attacks.
remediation: Configure X-Frame-Options or CSP frame directives to prevent unauthorized framing.

title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options
description: Browsers may incorrectly interpret file types, potentially enabling content-based attacks.
remediation: Set X-Content-Type-Options to 'nosniff' to enforce declared content types.

title: Directory Listing Enabled
description: Attackers may browse server directories and discover sensitive files or application structure.
remediation: Disable directory listing and restrict access to sensitive directories and resources.

title: Debug Mode Enabled
description: Debug functionality may expose internal application details useful to attackers.
remediation: Disable debug mode in production environments and restrict access to diagnostic information.

title: Verbose Error Messages
description: Detailed error messages may reveal application internals, system details, or sensitive information.
remediation: Display generic error messages to users and log detailed errors securely for administrators.

title: Insecure File Upload Configuration
description: Improper upload controls may allow attackers to upload malicious or executable files.
remediation: Validate file types, enforce size restrictions, scan uploads, and store files securely.

title: Path Traversal
description: Attackers may manipulate file paths to access files and directories outside intended locations.
remediation: Validate file paths, use allowlists, and restrict filesystem access permissions.

title: Local File Inclusion
description: Applications may include unintended local files, exposing sensitive information or functionality.
remediation: Validate file references and restrict inclusion to approved files only.

title: Remote File Inclusion
description: Attackers may load malicious files from remote sources, potentially leading to system compromise.
remediation: Disable remote file inclusion functionality and validate all file sources strictly.

title: Arbitrary File Upload
description: Attackers can upload unauthorized files that may execute code or compromise systems.
remediation: Implement strict upload validation, content inspection, and secure storage mechanisms.

title: Insecure Temporary Files
description: Sensitive information stored in temporary files may be accessible to unauthorized users.
remediation: Secure temporary storage locations and remove temporary files when no longer needed.

title: Unsafe Deserialization
description: Untrusted serialized data may allow attackers to execute code or manipulate application behavior.
remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data and use secure serialization formats with validation.

title: Unrestricted Resource Access
description: Resources are accessible without proper restrictions, exposing sensitive information or functionality.
remediation: Implement access controls, authentication requirements, and regular permission reviews.

title: Outdated Software Components
description: Older software versions may contain known vulnerabilities that can be exploited by attackers.
remediation: Maintain an inventory of software assets and regularly update components to supported versions.

title: Unsupported Operating System
description: Operating systems that no longer receive security updates are at increased risk of compromise.
remediation: Upgrade to supported operating systems and establish a lifecycle management process.

title: Missing Security Patches
description: Systems lacking critical security patches may remain vulnerable to publicly known exploits.
remediation: Implement a patch management program and apply security updates in a timely manner.

title: End-of-Life Software
description: End-of-life software no longer receives vendor support or security updates.
remediation: Replace unsupported software with actively maintained and supported alternatives.

title: Insecure Service Configuration
description: Services configured with insecure settings may expose systems to unauthorized access or attacks.
remediation: Review service configurations regularly and follow vendor security hardening guidelines.

title: Unnecessary Open Ports
description: Unused or unnecessary open ports increase the attack surface available to adversaries.
remediation: Close unused ports, disable unnecessary services, and restrict network exposure.

title: Weak Network Segmentation
description: Poor network segmentation allows attackers to move freely between systems after compromise.
remediation: Implement network segmentation, VLANs, and access control policies between environments.

title: Insecure Remote Access Configuration
description: Improperly secured remote access services may provide unauthorized entry points into the network.
remediation: Secure remote access with MFA, encryption, access restrictions, and continuous monitoring.

title: Telnet Usage
description: Telnet transmits credentials and data in plaintext, making interception attacks possible.
remediation: Replace Telnet with secure alternatives such as SSH for remote administration.

title: FTP Usage
description: FTP transmits data and credentials without encryption, exposing sensitive information.
remediation: Use secure protocols such as SFTP or FTPS for file transfers.

title: Anonymous FTP Access
description: Anonymous FTP access may expose files and services to unauthorized users.
remediation: Disable anonymous access and require authentication for all FTP services.

title: SMBv1 Enabled
description: SMBv1 contains known security weaknesses and has been exploited by major malware campaigns.
remediation: Disable SMBv1 and migrate to supported SMB versions with enhanced security.

title: Weak SNMP Community Strings
description: Weak or default SNMP community strings may allow unauthorized access to network information.
remediation: Use strong community strings or migrate to SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption.

title: Unsecured Network Shares
description: Improperly secured network shares may expose sensitive files to unauthorized users.
remediation: Restrict share permissions and review access rights regularly.

title: Insecure DNS Configuration
description: Misconfigured DNS services may leak information or facilitate spoofing attacks.
remediation: Restrict zone transfers, secure DNS infrastructure, and implement DNS security controls.

title: Unencrypted Network Protocols
description: Sensitive information transmitted over unencrypted protocols can be intercepted by attackers.
remediation: Use encrypted protocols such as HTTPS, SSH, TLS, and secure VPN technologies.

title: Public Cloud Storage Exposure
description: Cloud storage resources are publicly accessible, potentially exposing sensitive data.
remediation: Restrict public access, review permissions, and continuously monitor cloud storage configurations.

title: Misconfigured Cloud Permissions
description: Incorrect cloud access permissions may grant excessive access to users or services.
remediation: Review access policies regularly and enforce least-privilege principles.

title: Exposed Cloud Access Keys
description: Exposed cloud credentials may allow attackers to access and control cloud resources.
remediation: Rotate exposed keys immediately and store credentials in secure secret management systems.

title: Over-Permissive IAM Roles
description: IAM roles with excessive privileges increase the potential impact of account compromise.
remediation: Apply least-privilege access principles and regularly audit IAM role permissions.

title: Unrestricted Public Access
description: Resources exposed to unrestricted public access may be accessed or abused by unauthorized parties.
remediation: Restrict public exposure, enforce authentication requirements, and review access policies regularly.

title: Missing Risk Assessment
description: The document does not include a formal assessment of risks, threats, or potential business impacts.
remediation: Include a structured risk assessment identifying threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, and business impact.

title: Missing Executive Summary
description: The document lacks a high-level summary that provides key findings, objectives, and recommendations.
remediation: Add an executive summary section highlighting the purpose, findings, and major recommendations.

title: Missing Change Log
description: Changes made to the document are not tracked, reducing accountability and traceability.
remediation: Maintain a change log that records revisions, dates, authors, and modification details.

title: Missing References Section
description: The document does not identify supporting standards, frameworks, or information sources.
remediation: Include a references section listing standards, policies, guidelines, and external sources used.

title: Missing Version Control Information
description: Document version information is missing, making it difficult to identify the latest approved copy.
remediation: Add version numbers, revision dates, and version ownership details to the document.

title: Missing Approval Record
description: The document does not contain evidence of management review or formal approval.
remediation: Include approval records with reviewer names, roles, approval dates, and signatures if applicable.

title: Missing Security Classification
description: The document does not specify its security classification or handling requirements.
remediation: Clearly label the document with an appropriate security classification and handling instructions.

title: Missing Data Retention Policy
description: Requirements for retaining, archiving, or disposing of information are not documented.
remediation: Define retention periods, disposal procedures, and regulatory requirements for stored data.

title: Missing Incident Response Plan
description: The document does not describe procedures for identifying, reporting, and handling security incidents.
remediation: Include an incident response plan covering detection, containment, recovery, and reporting processes.

title: Missing Compliance Mapping
description: The document does not map controls or requirements to applicable standards and regulations.
remediation: Add a compliance mapping section linking requirements to relevant frameworks and regulations.

title: SNMPv1 Enabled
description: Legacy SNMPv1 is enabled on the device. SNMPv1 lacks encryption and cryptographic authentication, exposing network management traffic to sniffing and unauthorized modification.
remediation: Disable SNMPv1. Remove SNMPv1 host configurations and migrate monitoring systems to SNMPv3 with authPriv.

title: Permissive Firewall or ACL Rules
description: Access control lists (ACLs) or firewall rule sets terminate with over-permissive rules (such as permit ip any any), negating the security benefit of prior restrictions.
remediation: Replace catch-all permissive rules with explicit deny statements and log hits. Restrict allowed traffic to only required source and destination hosts.

title: Console Timeout Not Configured
description: Local console or interactive sessions do not have an idle timeout configured. Unattended active sessions can allow unauthorized physical access to the device management interface.
remediation: Configure a short idle timeout (5 minutes or less) for all local console and interactive terminal lines.
